abstracts.abstract: Software architecture documentation plays a critical role in maintaining system quality and facilitating communication among stakeholders. However, existing documentation approaches lack rigorous theoretical foundations for representing architectural decisions that evolve over time. This paper proposes a novel ontological framework called Architectural Decision Evolution Ontology (ADEO) that conceptualizes the temporal dynamics of software architecture. Drawing upon本体论 principles and grounding theory in empirical software engineering, we formalize the relationships between architectural decisions, their rationale, and environmental factors that trigger evolution. Our theoretical contribution includes a set of axioms defining decision dependency patterns, decay mechanisms, and refactoring triggers. We validate the framework through a longitudinal case study examining three large-scale industrial systems over five years, analyzing 847 architectural decisions. Results reveal that our ontology captures evolution patterns that existing frameworks cannot adequately represent, including cascading decision obsolescence and context-dependent stability characteristics. The ADEO framework enables architects to predict decision decay and proactively plan maintenance activities. This work represents a paradigm shift from static architectural documentation to dynamic decision-aware modeling, opening new research directions in software evolution theory and contributing to software quality assurance practices.

Software metrics serve as essential instruments for assessing code quality, yet existing complexity measures exhibit significant limitations when applied to modern software systems characterized by extensive use of design patterns and framework abstractions. This paper presents an enhanced suite of cognitive complexity metrics that extends the theoretical foundations established by prior work. We introduce the concept of structural depth inflation, a phenomenon where framework-induced indirection layers artificially elevate perceived complexity. Our analytical framework integrates code smell theory with cognitive load measurement to develop three novel metrics: Framework-Adjusted Cyclomatic Complexity (FACC), Pattern-Aware Structural Complexity (PASC), and Contextual Coupling Index (CCI). Through rigorous mathematical derivation and formal proofs of metric properties, we demonstrate that these measures exhibit superior correlation with maintenance effort compared to existing approaches. Empirical validation conducted across 2,340 Java projects from GitHub demonstrates that our metrics achieve 23% higher predictive accuracy for bug localization and 18% improvement in estimating refactoring effort. The proposed metrics contribute to software quality assessment by providing practitioners with theoretically grounded instruments that account for contemporary software development practices, thereby enhancing software reliability evaluation and reducing maintenance costs.

Continuous integration and deployment pipelines increasingly rely on automated testing, yet test suite optimization remains a critical challenge in software project management. We present TestOptima, a novel self-adaptive testing framework that fundamentally reimagines test prioritization through reinforcement learning. Unlike existing approaches that rely on static prioritization strategies or historical failure correlations, TestOptima employs a multi-armed bandit framework with contextual awareness of code changes, test dependencies, and deployment risk profiles. The system architecture comprises three integrated components: a change impact analyzer utilizing abstract syntax tree diffing, a risk assessment engine incorporating historical reliability data, and an adaptive prioritization agent that continuously learns from deployment outcomes. We implemented TestOptima as an open-source plugin integrated with Jenkins and GitLab CI, evaluating its effectiveness across 18 industrial projects spanning telecommunications, finance, and healthcare domains. Results demonstrate that TestOptima reduces mean time to failure detection by 47% while decreasing total pipeline execution time by 31% compared to state-of-the-art approaches. The framework exemplifies a paradigm shift toward learning-based testing strategies that adapt to organizational contexts, representing a significant advancement in software testing automation and contributing to more efficient software processes.

Security vulnerability detection in software systems requires increasingly sophisticated analysis techniques, yet current static analysis tools suffer from high false positive rates that undermine developer trust and efficiency. This paper introduces VulnScope, an enhanced static analysis platform that significantly improves vulnerability detection accuracy through hybrid analysis techniques. The system combines scalable lightweight static analysis with targeted dynamic symbolic execution, orchestrated through a novel triage engine that intelligently routes code segments to appropriate analysis modes based on complexity indicators and historical precision data. VulnScope incorporates a machine learning classifier trained on vulnerability patterns from 12,000 CVEs to prioritize findings and suppress unlikely positives. The architecture includes four major components: a preprocessing module for code normalization, a scalable static analyzer based on points-to analysis, a constraint solver for symbolic execution, and a Bayesian network-based prioritization system. We evaluated VulnScope against leading tools including SpotBugs, CodeQL, and SonarQube using the NIST SARD dataset containing 140,000 test cases, achieving a 34% reduction in false positives while maintaining equivalent detection recall. Case studies with three Fortune 500 companies demonstrate that VulnScope reduces security review time by 41% and improves software security assessment workflows, contributing substantially to software reliability and quality assurance in enterprise contexts.
